city.name: Washington, DC
city.regionLabel: Washington, DC, Northern Virginia, suburban Maryland and a sensible drive
city.coreLabel: DC / Northern Virginia / suburban Maryland core

events.title: Asia After Dark: Diwali Festival
events.priceLabel: Check source for admission details; advance registration recommended; food extra
events.description: Celebrate the festival of lights with crafts, South Asian performances and illuminated museum spaces. Family activities run early, followed by DJ MAIYA’s plaza dance party from 7:30 PM; advance registration is recommended.

events.title: BSO: Shéhérazade & Sibelius
events.priceLabel: Check source for ticket prices and fees
events.description: Jonathon Heyward leads the Baltimore Symphony Orchestra in Ravel’s Shéhérazade and Sibelius’s Second Symphony, with mezzo-soprano Fleur Barron. Friday is the Strathmore performance; the Sunday presentation of this program is in Baltimore.

events.title: Cox Farms Fall Festival: Final Weekend
events.priceLabel: $15 ages 2+; online tickets required; under 2 free
events.description: Take advantage of the festival’s lower-priced final Friday for hayrides, slides and other farm attractions. Tickets must be bought online, and the last entry is an hour before closing.

events.title: Creative Aging: Closing Weekend
events.priceLabel: Museum admission $20; ages 18 and under free; check gallery access details
events.description: See artwork made through the Phillips’ creative-aging programs, including programs for older adults with memory loss. The exhibition closes Sunday; the listed price is general museum admission, and the museum also offers some free ground-floor spaces.

events.title: Fall Exhibitions at the American University Museum
events.venue: American University Museum, Katzen Arts Center
events.priceLabel: Free; garage parking fees may apply
events.description: Explore the university museum’s fall group of exhibitions, with painting, calligraphy and photography among the offerings. It is a quieter free museum option northwest of downtown, with several shows available in one visit.

events.title: Frida… A Self Portrait: Closing Weekend
events.priceLabel: Check source for ticket prices; very limited availability
events.age: Check source for age and content guidance
events.description: Vanessa Severo’s solo performance explores Frida Kahlo’s life and art in a 75-minute show without intermission. Availability was very limited when checked; confirm your exact performance before planning around it.

events.title: Hundred Days: Closing Weekend
events.priceLabel: Adult $65 + $5 fee; senior/student $55 + $5 fee
events.age: Mature themes; check source for guidance
events.description: This intimate folk-punk musical turns a real love story into a meditation on the time people have together. Friday opens the final weekend of Keegan’s run; the performance lasts about 75 minutes without intermission.

events.title: Much Here Is Beautiful: Bicentennial Photography
events.address: 8th and G Streets NW, Washington, DC
events.priceLabel: Free
events.description: See how photographers documented American places and communities around the 1976 bicentennial. This temporary exhibition offers a useful counterpoint to the current anniversary year, with late-afternoon museum hours that suit a relaxed visit.

events.title: On Stage: Portraying the Performing Arts
events.address: 8th and G Streets NW, Washington, DC
events.priceLabel: Free
events.description: A new exhibition brings performers into focus through portraiture, including figures from theater, jazz and hip-hop. This is its opening weekend, and the gallery’s evening hours make it an easy addition to a Penn Quarter outing.

events.title: Routed West: African American Quilts in California
events.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts
events.address: 1250 New York Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20005
events.priceLabel: Adult $16; DC resident/senior $13; ages 21 and under free
events.description: Follow the movement of quiltmaking traditions from the American South to California through work by African American women. Allow time to look closely at the textiles and the family histories behind them; this is a paid-admission museum weekend.
events.sourceName: National Museum of Women in the Arts

events.title: To Hear Her Speak: Black Women and Shakespeare
events.address: 201 East Capitol Street SE, Washington, DC 20003
events.priceLabel: Free; $15 donation suggested; timed passes recommended
events.description: Discover how Black women have interpreted and reshaped Shakespeare through an exhibition of books, photographs and other objects. Bring headphones for the audio content, and reserve a free timed entry if you want a more predictable visit.

events.title: Adams Morgan Fall PorchFest
events.venue: Porches and stages across Adams Morgan
events.address: Adams Morgan; Marie Reed stage at 2201 18th Street NW, Washington, DC
events.priceLabel: Free; food and drink purchases extra
events.description: Follow the neighborhood’s stage map for a free afternoon of local bands on porches and outdoor stages. Pick a few nearby stops rather than trying to cover the whole festival, and check the organizer’s lineup before setting out.

events.title: Czech Christmas Market
events.address: 3900 Spring of Freedom Street NW, Washington, DC 20008
events.priceLabel: Free; individual timed RSVP and photo ID required
events.description: Browse Czech glass, ornaments and traditional treats at the embassy’s annual market. Reserve a named entry slot for each guest and bring photo ID; the embassy prohibits large bags and pets, and some vendors take cash only.

events.title: D.C. United vs. New York City FC
events.priceLabel: Check source for ticket prices and fees
events.age: All ages; check stadium entry policy
events.description: D.C. United closes its regular season with a home Decision Day match against New York City FC. The club also celebrates its supporters at this Fan Appreciation match; check official tickets for current seat availability.

events.title: Red Baraat
events.priceLabel: Check source for ticket prices and fees
events.description: Red Baraat brings Punjabi rhythms together with jazz, hip-hop, funk and go-go for an energetic night at the Barns. Allow time for arrival before the 8 PM show; parking is included at the venue.

events.title: Afternoon on the Pontoon
events.venue: Black Hill Discovery Center / Little Seneca Lake
events.priceLabel: $7 per person; registration required
events.description: Take a guided pontoon outing on Little Seneca Lake to look for wildlife from the water. Meet at the pontoon dock near the boat-rental area, dress for the weather and bring a jacket for the cooler conditions on the lake.

events.title: Arlington FRESHFARM Market
events.priceLabel: Check source; food and other purchases extra
events.description: Build a relaxed neighborhood morning around seasonal produce, baked goods and other regional foods from local vendors. The organizer’s current annual schedule includes this weekend; bring a bag and check the market page for vendor updates.

events.title: Cox Farms Fall Festival: Final Weekend
events.priceLabel: $25 ages 2+; online tickets required; under 2 free
events.description: Pumpkin Madness joins Cox Farms’ final weekend, adding pumpkin destruction to the fall-festival attractions. Book online before driving out and arrive before the 4 PM last-entry cutoff.

events.title: Creative Aging: Closing Weekend
events.priceLabel: Museum admission $20; ages 18 and under free; check gallery access details

events.title: DC Beer Festival
events.address: 1500 South Capitol Street SE, Washington, DC 20003
events.priceLabel: General admission $55; food extra; check source for fees
events.description: Sample beers from a broad lineup of breweries inside the ballpark, with live music and dueling pianos between tastings. Choose one session; general admission includes beer samples, while food is sold separately.

events.title: DMV Chocolate & Coffee Festival
events.priceLabel: Online $17.99 + $0.45 fee through Nov 6; $20 door; under 12 free with paid adult
events.description: Make a tasting day of coffee, chocolate and specialty foods at the indoor fieldhouse. Saturday has the longer public session and a separately ticketed VIP early hour; the advance general-admission price ends late Friday.

events.title: Downtown Silver Spring FRESHFARM Market
events.address: Veterans Plaza, 1 Veterans Place, Silver Spring, MD 20910
events.priceLabel: Check source; food and other purchases extra
events.description: Build a relaxed neighborhood morning around seasonal produce, baked goods and other regional foods from local vendors. The organizer’s current annual schedule includes this weekend; bring a bag and check the market page for vendor updates.

events.title: Evening Campfire: Owls
events.priceLabel: $10; adults and children ages 3+ must register
events.description: Gather around an evening fire to learn about local owls, with marshmallows provided and the possibility of a short hike. An adult must register alongside each child; the program is outdoors, so come dressed for a November night.

events.title: Maryland Emancipation Day at Oakley Cabin
events.venue: Oakley Cabin African American Museum and Park
events.priceLabel: Free
events.description: Hear stories and explore hands-on activities at Oakley Cabin’s free commemoration. Short cabin tours and readings of the Reconstruction Amendments run through the afternoon, making it possible to join for part of the program.

events.title: Maryland Emancipation Day at Woodlawn Manor
events.time: 10:00 AM–4:00 PM; lecture 11:00 AM; hike 1:00–2:30 PM
events.priceLabel: Museum free; optional lecture $8; guided hike $10 adult / $8 child or senior
events.description: Visit the museum free for Maryland Emancipation Day, with separately ticketed options for a morning lecture and an afternoon Underground Railroad trail hike. Register for the paid programs ahead of time; the park recommends doing so by Friday noon.

events.title: National Philharmonic: Postcards from America
events.priceLabel: Check source for ticket prices and fees
events.description: Daniel Hege conducts a program featuring Copland’s Appalachian Spring, Joan Tower’s Made in America and music by Barber, Gershwin and Márquez. Soprano Danielle Talamantes joins National Philharmonic for this American-themed concert.

events.venue: National Gallery of Art, West Building
events.address: 6th Street and Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20565
events.priceLabel: Free; no passes or tickets required
events.description: Explore early photographs of Black Americans in this new National Gallery exhibition opening Saturday. The portraits offer personal encounters with nineteenth- and early twentieth-century lives; admission is free, without a timed pass.

events.address: 201 East Capitol Street SE, Washington, DC 20003
events.priceLabel: Public $30; members $25; check source for fees
events.description: Go deeper into the Folger’s exhibition on Black women and Shakespeare at a special evening curator’s talk. This separately ticketed Reading Room event complements the free gallery exhibition; reserve the talk itself in advance.

events.title: DMV Chocolate & Coffee Festival
events.priceLabel: Online $17.99 + $0.45 fee through Nov 6; $20 door; under 12 free with paid adult
events.description: Sunday’s shorter session offers another chance to explore coffee roasters, chocolatiers and specialty-food vendors. Children under 12 enter free with a paying adult; check the organizer for ticket availability and any tasting details.

events.priceLabel: Adult $65 + $5 fee; senior/student $55 + $5 fee
events.age: Mature themes; check source for guidance
events.description: Catch the final matinee of Keegan’s folk-punk musical about love and making the most of limited time. The 75-minute, no-intermission format leaves room for an early dinner around Dupont Circle afterward.

events.title: Maryland Emancipation Day at Harper Cabin
events.venue: Thomas Harper Cabin at Brookside Nature Center
events.priceLabel: Free
events.description: Visit Thomas Harper Cabin for a free afternoon of local African American history, hands-on activities and short tours. Readings of the Reconstruction Amendments take place on the hour, followed by cabin tours at the half-hour.

events.title: Remember Me: Opening Weekend
events.venue: National Gallery of Art, West Building
events.address: 6th Street and Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20565
events.priceLabel: Free; no passes or tickets required
events.description: The exhibition’s first Sunday is a chance to linger over early photographic portraits of Black Americans. Find it in the West Building’s ground-floor galleries and pair the visit with the museum’s permanent collection.

events.title: Cox Farms Fall Festival: Final Weekend
events.priceLabel: $25 ages 2+; online tickets required; under 2 free
events.description: The season ends Sunday with Pumpkin Madness and the farm’s fall attractions. This is the final chance for 2026, so buy the dated ticket online and leave enough time before the 4 PM entry cutoff.

events.venue: Black Hill Discovery Center / Little Seneca Lake

events.description: Paddle Little Seneca Lake with a naturalist on this guided morning tour. Boats, paddles and life jackets are provided, but this is not a beginner lesson: participants need basic kayaking experience and should register for a place.
